text.LookupChainedMapSentence: In the chained pattern the hash map is slower than the original arithmetic it replaces (325 ns against 188 ns)
text.LookupConclusionPhrase: in the pattern of the matrix product it was slower than the original arithmetic
text.SeqSmallestSentence: at N = 100 the cached program is only 1.3 times faster (0.295 s against 0.374 s)
text.SeqGainSentence: The speedup grows with the matrix up to N = 800 and is about the same at N = 1000 (25.0 and 24.7)
text.SeqMemoryCrossoverSentence: For very small matrices the cached program therefore uses more memory than the original; in our runs it uses less from N = 200 upward
text.SeqReferenceNote: We did not run the original library at these sizes. If its run time keeps growing with N^3 from N = 1000, our largest run of it, the original would need about 6 h 43 min at N = 4000 on this machine. That figure is an extrapolation, not a measurement. At N = 4000 the cached program needs 19 min 42 s and 0.13 GiB here, against 20 min 16 s and 0.53 GB in the assignment text, which was measured on a different processor.
text.SeqRunsPhrase: 1 to 5 runs per size; the table gives the median
text.SeqRepeatSentence: Where a size was run more than once, the slowest run took up to 9% longer than the fastest for runs under 10 s, and up to 4% longer for longer runs.
text.MpiNodesLimitation: The processes ran on 4 machines of one cluster. Another network, or other machines, will give a different break-even point.
text.MpiNodesSentence: The processes ran on up to 4 different machines, so the broadcasts crossed the network
text.MpiBreakEvenSentence: With 4 processes the smallest tested size at which MPI was faster is N=100, and it stayed faster at every larger size
text.MpiWinsSentence: The margin at N=100 is small, though: the ratio is 1.07, one determinant takes 2.0 ms, and MPI won 5 of the 6 runs. At N=75 MPI was slower, with a ratio of 0.76, and from N=150 on, where the ratio is 1.43, it won every run. The break-even therefore lies between N=75 and N=150, and our runs do not place it more exactly.
text.MpiConclusionSentence: With 4 processes the smallest tested size at which MPI was faster is N = 100, by a margin of 7% that is within the spread between runs; from N = 150 upward it won every run, and at N = 2000 it is 3.74 times as fast
text.MpiOneProcessSentence: At N = 2000 the single-process run is 1.06 times as fast as the sequential program, without any parallelism.
text.MpiRepeatsSentence: Every configuration was timed 3 times on each of the two matrices
text.MpiAbstractSentence: With 4 processes across 4 machines, the smallest tested size at which the MPI program is faster than the cached sequential program is N = 100, by 7% in the median; from N = 150 upward it is faster in every run.
text.MpiNoiseSentence: The same sequential determinant was timed in several jobs. The medians of those jobs differ by up to a factor of 2.2 for determinants shorter than 0.1 s and by up to 3% for longer ones, so ratios close to 1 carry little meaning.
text.MpiBlockSentence: The table repeats the measurement for other panel widths. At N = 1000 the ratio lies between 2.28 and 3.54 for all 5 widths. The choice matters most at N = 100, where b = 1 reaches 0.30 and b = 8 reaches 1.07.
text.MpiReferenceSentence: The two were not timed on the same machine, so we do not compare them.
